events.title: Treat malformed send acknowledgements as unconfirmed
events.body:
After the POST, verify that the decoded response is a JSON object before calling `.get()`. A valid JSON response such as `null` or `[]` currently raises `AttributeError`, bypassing the explicit unconfirmed-outcome error. Raise the existing reconciliation-required `RuntimeError` for these responses, since the message may already have been sent. Critic pass: do not classify malformed acknowledgements as retryable; that could duplicate an owner-visible message.
With mocked configuration and health checks, return `null` and `[]` from the send POST. Assert that each raises the reconciliation-required `RuntimeError` and that exactly one POST was made. Also verify that a valid acknowledgement still returns its message ID. This claim is falsified if malformed acknowledgements already produce that error, or if the regression shows a change in successful delivery behavior.
The regression is proposed from the supplied source and has not been run. Callers must still honor the reconciliation-required error and avoid automatically retrying it.

events.title: Validate WhatsApp response shapes before reading fields
events.body:
Ji An: Add explicit dictionary checks after decoding health and send responses. A non-object health response should raise WhatsAppUnavailable before POST; a non-object send acknowledgement should raise the existing unconfirmed-outcome RuntimeError. Evidence: valid JSON such as null or [] currently reaches .get() and raises an uncaught AttributeError.
Use mocked HTTP responses and a temporary valid configuration, with no network. For health bodies null, [], and "connected", assert WhatsAppUnavailable and zero POST calls. For the same malformed acknowledgement shapes after valid health, assert RuntimeError and exactly one POST. Include a successful acknowledgement control. These are proposed regressions, not executed tests.
Critic pass: response validation cannot establish whether a POST delivered or prevent duplicates. Revised proposal preserves the existing no-retry rule after POST and all live defaults. The claim is falsified if malformed health responses already produce WhatsAppUnavailable or malformed acknowledgements already produce the specified RuntimeError without this change.

events.title: Classify malformed send acknowledgements as unconfirmed
events.body:
A valid JSON response such as null or [] makes result.get raise AttributeError after the POST, bypassing the explicit reconciliation error. Add an isinstance(result, dict) guard before acknowledgement checks and raise the existing RuntimeError for non-object responses. Preserve the no-automatic-retry policy.
Use a temporary valid configuration and mocked urlopen responses: connected health with the expected session, then a send response containing null or []. Assert RuntimeError with 'reconcile before retry' and exactly one POST. Include a successful object acknowledgement control. No network is needed. The defect claim is falsified if the current code already produces that RuntimeError for these fixtures.
Small change to error classification; it does not establish whether delivery occurred. Do not classify malformed POST responses as WhatsAppUnavailable, since that would imply sending is safe to retry.

events.title: Validate WhatsApp JSON objects before field access
events.body:
Add explicit isinstance(value, dict) checks after decoding config, health, and send acknowledgements in send() and status(). Raise ValueError for invalid config/health inside existing try blocks; treat non-object acknowledgements as missing acknowledgements. Evidence: valid JSON such as null or [] currently reaches .get() or string-key indexing and can escape as AttributeError or TypeError. Critic pass: guarding send() alone leaves status() vulnerable, so apply the same validation there.
Use mocked config reads and urlopen responses; no network. Parameterize null, [], "text", 0, and true. In send(), invalid config must raise WhatsAppUnavailable with zero HTTP calls; invalid health must raise WhatsAppUnavailable with no POST; invalid acknowledgement must raise RuntimeError mentioning reconciliation after exactly one POST, with no retry. In status(), invalid config must return not_paired and invalid health must return disconnected. Retain successful object-response controls. The claim is falsified if any case leaks AttributeError/TypeError, sends after invalid preflight data, retries a POST, or changes valid-response behavior.
Minimal compatibility risk: these response locations already require object fields. Preserve session checks, ambiguous-send handling, and live model defaults. This is a proposal based on supplied source; tests were not executed.

events.title: Validate WhatsApp response shapes at each delivery stage
events.body:
Ji An’s proposal improves on my send-only proposal and the critic’s by also covering malformed health responses before delivery. The regression proposal identifies an additional status() failure: non-object configuration or health JSON can raise AttributeError. Its proposed scope is strongest, but configuration and health validation must occur inside the existing exception-handling blocks to produce the stated results. In send(), classify invalid preflight data as WhatsAppUnavailable and a non-object POST acknowledgement as reconciliation-required RuntimeError. Preserve the no-retry rule after POST.
With mocked file reads and HTTP responses, test JSON null, [], "text", 0, and true at each boundary. Invalid send configuration must cause zero HTTP calls; invalid health must cause zero POSTs; invalid acknowledgements must cause exactly one POST and a reconciliation-required RuntimeError. For status(), expect not_paired for invalid configuration and disconnected for invalid health. Include valid health and acknowledgement controls. These tests are proposed, not executed.
The source supports the failure claim, but no regression has been run. Response validation cannot determine whether a POST delivered; callers must reconcile ambiguous outcomes before retrying. No live defaults need to change.

events.title: Validate response shapes while preserving delivery uncertainty
events.body:
Ji Eun and critic identify the same supported defect: non-object POST JSON reaches .get() and leaks AttributeError. Ji An additionally covers malformed health responses. The regression proposal usefully covers status(), but overstates send() configuration failures: its existing TypeError handler already handles the listed non-object configurations. Revised proposal: validate object shapes in health and acknowledgement handling and in status(); preserve existing session checks and post-send reconciliation errors. No evidence establishes improved delivery rates or duplicate prevention.
Without network, mock configuration reads and urlopen. Parameterize null, [], "text", 0, and true. Assert malformed health raises WhatsAppUnavailable with zero POSTs; malformed acknowledgements raise RuntimeError containing 'reconcile before retry' after exactly one POST; malformed status configuration returns not_paired and malformed status health returns disconnected. Include valid controls and malformed JSON controls. Run against baseline and revision: the expected baseline AttributeError followed by the specified revised behavior is decisive evidence. Tests are proposed, not executed.
Error normalization does not establish delivery outcome or ensure callers avoid retries. Keep ambiguous POST failures non-retryable and all live defaults unchanged. A passing revised regression supports the narrow error-handling claim only.

events.title: Validate JSON shapes while preserving delivery uncertainty
events.body:
The supplied source confirms non-object health and send responses can leak AttributeError through .get(). status() also fails on non-object config or health. Prefer explicit dictionary guards with existing error classifications. Ji Eun and critic correctly address acknowledgements but omit preflight and status failures; Ji An covers preflight but omits status. The regression proposal is broader, but send() already catches TypeError from non-object config indexing, so those cases are coverage rather than a demonstrated new fix.
Mock file reads and HTTP responses without network. Parameterize null, [], strings, numbers, and booleans. Assert malformed health raises WhatsAppUnavailable with zero POSTs; malformed send acknowledgements raise RuntimeError containing 'reconcile before retry' after exactly one POST; malformed status config/health returns not_paired/disconnected. Include valid delivery and wrong-session controls. The current-source defect is demonstrated by AttributeError; any such exception after revision means the fix failed, rather than falsifying the original defect claim.
Tests were not executed. Explicit shape checks are preferable to broadly catching AttributeError, which could hide programming errors. Error normalization alone does not prove callers avoid retries or improve delivery rates; caller behavior is not supplied. Preserve all live defaults and never classify an ambiguous POST outcome as retryable.

events.title: Validate JSON object shapes at WhatsApp boundaries
events.body:
Add isinstance(value, dict) guards after decoding config and health in both send() and status(). Raise ValueError inside their existing try blocks: send() then raises WhatsAppUnavailable; status() returns not_paired for invalid config or disconnected for invalid health. For acknowledgements, prepend `not isinstance(result, dict) or` to the existing missing-acknowledgement condition. Critique: Ji Eun and critic cover only acknowledgements; Ji An also covers health but omits config and status(). The regression proposal covers all boundaries but overstates the current send-config defect: non-object config already raises caught TypeError. Broadly catching AttributeError is an alternative, but explicit shape guards are narrower.
Proposed, not executed: parameterize JSON null, [], "text", 0, and true using mocked file reads and urlopen; make unexpected HTTP calls fail immediately. Invalid send config must raise WhatsAppUnavailable with zero HTTP calls; invalid health must do so after one health request and zero POSTs. Invalid acknowledgements must raise RuntimeError containing 'reconcile before retry' after exactly one POST. For status(), invalid config must return not_paired without HTTP; invalid health must return disconnected. Include valid-object controls for successful delivery, connected status, disabled config, and wrong-session rejection. Decisive criterion: all shapes produce the specified outcomes without leaked AttributeError/TypeError, extra POSTs, or changed valid-object behavior.
Shape validation cannot determine whether a POST delivered. Preserve reconciliation-required failures after POST, the existing session check, and live defaults. Evidence is limited to the supplied source; no tools, code, or tests were executed.

events.title: Validate WhatsApp JSON object shapes
events.body:
Select a small repair: validate decoded configuration and health objects within their existing error-handling blocks, and treat a non-object POST acknowledgement as an unconfirmed outcome requiring reconciliation. Non-object send configuration is already handled by the existing TypeError catch; its test is a control, not evidence of a new defect. Preserve session checks, the no-automatic-retry rule, and live defaults.
Proposed, not run: mock file reads and HTTP responses without network access. Parameterize null, [], "text", 0, and true. Assert invalid send configuration makes zero HTTP calls; invalid health raises WhatsAppUnavailable with zero POSTs; and an invalid acknowledgement raises a reconciliation-required RuntimeError after exactly one POST. Assert invalid status configuration returns not_paired and invalid status health returns disconnected. Include successful delivery, connected status, disabled configuration, and wrong-session controls. Compare baseline and revised behavior; the repair fails if the specified classifications or valid controls do not hold.
The supplied source supports the shape-handling defect, but no test has run. A malformed acknowledgement cannot establish whether delivery occurred, and this repair cannot ensure callers reconcile before retrying.

events.title: Approved
events.body: The change correctly handles non-object JSON while preserving delivery safety: malformed configuration or health prevents POST, and malformed acknowledgements require reconciliation after one POST. Status checks return defined states instead of leaking AttributeError. The deterministic, network-free regression meaningfully checks exception classification, request counts and ordering, payload preservation, and success/session/disabled controls. Some configuration cases already passed because TypeError was caught, but the remaining cases expose real failures in the original code. Assessment is based on the supplied code and tests; no tools were run.

events.title: Approved
events.body: The guards correctly classify non-object JSON: configuration and health failures prevent POSTs, while malformed acknowledgements require reconciliation after sending. Status now returns defined fallback states instead of raising AttributeError. The deterministic, network-free regression checks exception classification, request counts and methods, payload preservation, and valid/disabled/wrong-session controls. This meaningfully tests the change without altering delivery defaults. Test-run results are supplied, not independently verified.

outcome: The original failed the new regression, the candidate passed, and both reviewers approved.
